prompts.task:
$splunk-configure

Work in ./service. Copy otel-audit.json to .observe/otel-audit.json first. I accept the six metrics in that audit as source-only inputs for detector design. Generate detector Terraform and its reports, applying the skill’s route-level de-duplication. Do not use the network or run Terraform. Emission and remote SignalFlow validation remain unproven.

judge_inputs: Inspect ./service/.observe for the resulting files when present, especially ./service/.observe/terraform/detectors.tf, ./service/.observe/terraform/variables.tf, ./service/.observe/detectors.md, and ./service/.observe/splunk-configure-verify.md.
Read ./last_message.md for the agent final response.
Read ./trace.jsonl for the exact shell commands the agent ran.
rubric:
Rule: Read the canonical audit and classify its accepted source-only metrics. Use http.server.request.duration for a P99 latency threshold and cover at least one of throughput or saturation.
Example: Use http.server.request.duration for a P99 latency threshold; its observation count can support throughput.
Evidence: Inspect classification, generated resources and source metric names. http.server.active_requests can supply saturation.
Insufficient evidence: Ignoring all metrics because runtime proof is unavailable despite explicit source-only acceptance, or inventing emission proof.

Rule: Merge metrics that describe the same route outcome. The payment error counter must not create a duplicate detector.
Example: For POST /payment errors, use http.server.request.duration with its error.type attribute.
Evidence: The error detector uses the histogram; checkout.payment.errors may be documented as merged but has no separate detector resource distinguished only by metric name.
Insufficient evidence: A separate payment-counter detector duplicating the same route outcome.

Rule: Give each signalfx_detector a name, SignalFlow program, service filter using var.service_name and a rule with a supported severity. Scope the payment error detector to both the route and failing outcome.
Example: Filter payment errors by service.name, http.route=/payment and error.type=*; the latency detector remains distinct.
Evidence: Inspect .observe/terraform/detectors.tf, including each program_text and Critical/Major/Minor/Warning rule. Threshold or baseline detection is acceptable.
Insufficient evidence: A payment error detector aggregating every route, missing resources or severities, or invalid detection logic.

Rule: Each detector must aggregate and publish its metric stream, then include actual threshold or baseline detection.
Example: Use data(..., filter=filter('service.name', ...)).<aggregation>().publish(), followed by detect(when(...)) or an against_recent/alerts_and_clears baseline.
Evidence: Inspect the executable SignalFlow expression for each detector and whether its method fits the category.
Insufficient evidence: A publish-only chart expression with no detection logic.

Rule: Make credentials sensitive and provide at least one threshold or baseline tuning variable per detector. Write variables.tf and terraform.tfvars.example.
Example: Declare realm, sensitive api_token and service_name, plus a threshold or baseline tuning variable for every detector.
Evidence: Inspect variables, example values and references from program_text.
Insufficient evidence: Real hardcoded tokens, a literal service name in detector programs, or no per-detector tuning.

Rule: Explain generated detectors, metrics, severity and classification decisions, then give a clear publishing handoff.
Example: Point the reviewer to a later Terraform apply or $splunk-detector-publish step without executing it.
Evidence: Read .observe/detectors.md and inspect actual commands. Keep source-only acceptance, unproven emission and unavailable remote validation explicit.
Insufficient evidence: Network execution, the retired $splunk-sync alias, or a source-only design presented as verified emission.

Rule: List every generated detector in the configure verification report with its resource label or name, metric and severity.
Example: A latency row names latency_http_server_request_duration, its histogram and Warning severity.
Evidence: Compare .observe/splunk-configure-verify.md with the Terraform resources. Full condition text is useful but optional.
Insufficient evidence: A general completion claim with no detector checklist.

Rule: Use the saved canonical audit and related instrumentation evidence. Preserve the existing audit HTML and its selection tray.
Example: Read .observe/otel-audit.json rather than rerunning instrumentation to obtain the requested detector inputs.
Evidence: Inspect actual reads, commands and changes to .observe artifacts.
Insufficient evidence: Rerunning an instrumentation prompt or modifying .observe/otel.html.

Rule: Run the bundled configure validator after generation and reflect its actual result. A failed validator means configure failure.
Example: Supply the exact accepted source-only metric names to the validator; record that Terraform and remote compilation were not run.
Evidence: Inspect commands, validator output and .observe/splunk-configure-verify.md for the generated Terraform and both reports.
Insufficient evidence: An unrun or skipped check called passing, an ignored validator failure, or a claim that terraform validate ran.

Rule: Keep infrastructure changes outside this skill. This task also forbids every Terraform command and all network calls.
Example: A report can describe a later apply command while the actor performs only local generation and permitted validation.
Evidence: Inspect trace.jsonl for actual commands. The skill’s usual read-only Terraform allowance is limited to version, fmt, init, validate and plan; none is authorized in this task.
Insufficient evidence: Executing terraform apply, terraform destroy, any other Terraform command here, or a network call.

Rule: Keep generated project files under ./service/.observe/.
Example: Write detector files to .observe/terraform and reports to .observe.
Evidence: Inspect the actual generated and modified file inventory. The skill’s static tool-permission declarations are checked separately by ordinary tests.
Insufficient evidence: A new project file outside .observe, even if the detector output is otherwise correct.
